label: early original-phase token right after t/s, in sequences starting with n/w/c
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.009% of steps). 99% of mass is in the original (input) phase, at positions t=2..5 (peak t=3), on the token that immediately follows a t (73% of mass) or s (18%). It is further concentrated in sequences whose first token is n, w or c (84% of mass) and on current tokens a, z, w, r, h. Top examples: n w s t [h], n 2 2 t [a], n w t [z], c v t t [a]. Magnitude is highest for n-initial prefixes containing w/2 followed by t. It essentially never fires in the delimiter or copy phases, at t=0-1 or t>=8. The predicate captures ~74% of activation mass but with very low precision (~4%): the feature depends on a specific prefix combination (a hashed-looking conjunction of first token, preceding t/s and current token) that simple predicates do not isolate; the tightest conjunction tried reaches only F1 ~0.26.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+5.32), prev_tok=t (+4.47), prev_tok=s (+3.65), in_tok=a (+3.35), prev2_tok=w (+3.24), orig0=c (+3.12). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.71), orig_idx=-1 (-2.78), prev2_tok=n (-1.92).
